summary: Tent cabin on Nesmith Point (Multnomah Co., OR) in 1929, a 14x14 lookout on a 12-foot tower by 1934, gone by 1963; no source describes the site today.

facts.design: Tent cabin (1929), then a standard 14 x 14 lookout station on a 12-foot tower (1934); the register calls the cab an L-4
facts.status_note: Cab removed around 1959 to 1963 per sources; Wikipedia says destroyed; one hike guide mentions an old fire lookout on the climb, unconfirmed. No source describes the site now in detail.

access.note: On foot only: the one road into the peak runs through the closed Bull Run Watershed, so legal access is by trail (Wikipedia).

visit.trail_note: Trail #428 climbs from an Interstate 84 frontage road. Friends of the Columbia Gorge lists the out-and-back hike at 10.2 miles with about 3,700 feet of gain, rated expert.

events.note: Tent cabin erected on the site
October 1934 notice: standard 14 x 14 lookout station on a 12-foot tower being completed; register and firelookout.com say an L-4 cab replaced the tent in the 1930s
Road joining the Larch Mountain and Oak Grove roads recently finished, with a branch to the station; CCC crew from Latourelle Prairie camp helped with new buildings in September
CCC crew working on the Nesmith Point Trail at Warrendale (May 1937)
Planned line change (August 1937): Nesmith Point and other stations to be served through Eagle Creek and Tanner Butte instead of Indian Mountain
Coast and Geodetic Survey described the survey station as the finial of the Forest Service lookout house on Nesmith Point
Survey station recovered in good condition
Lookout removed, circa 1959, per the Oregon lookout history
Gone by 1963 per the register; firelookout.com gives Gone 1963
Registered in the Former Fire Lookout Sites register on August 26, 2010 (US 619)

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Oregon lookout history gives a circa 1959 removal, while the register and firelookout.com give 1963 as the date it was gone. The story reports both and calls 1959 an estimate.

Wikipedia says the lookout was destroyed and the register says gone, but a hike guide describes an old fire lookout and outhouse on the climb. No source confirms what stands there, so the story marks the guide's claim as unconfirmed.

notes_for_editor: Brief access was unknown; filled from Wikipedia and the Friends hike guide. Brief height 3.7 m matches the 12-foot tower in the October 1934 notice. Elevation differs by source: 3,880 ft (register), 3,872 ft (firelookout.com), 3,848 ft (Wikipedia peak); not used in the story. No staffing roster or fire events found; staffing left as unknown with the 1937 line-change note only. The register's 1963 and the Oregon history's c.1959 are both kept. The hike guide's old fire lookout is the main open question; a dated photo or a Forest Service check would settle it. No new photos captured (firetower.org captions present but image URLs were not in the cached text).
